claims.claim: Intersect requests 1,193,000 ADA, described as $298,250, to support Technical Steering Committee activities for 12 months.
The budget is allocated as 256,000 ADA for WP1, 832,000 ADA for WP2, and 105,000 ADA for WP3.
WP2 funds the Parameter Committee, CIP editors, and Hard Fork Working Group to support protocol governance and evolution.
WP3 will establish a pilot independent technical review programme launching in 2027 with conflict-of-interest provisions, published recusals, and open reviewer selection against documented criteria.
The proposal states all expenditure will be fully accounted for and any unspent funds returned to the Cardano treasury.
The proposal states the work is contingent on approval of the IntersectMBO budget proposal.
The proposal states it achieved the required 67% support threshold during the 2026 Intersect Budget Process Hydra Voting phase and provides references to voting materials and audited results.

The proposal states the requested amount does not breach the applicable 350M ADA Net Change Limit covering Epoch 613 to Epoch 713 at the moment of submission and links to the related governance action.

Independent audits and assurance for the proposal will be provided by Appold, with possible reviews including deliverable verification, control testing, spend validation, and milestone evidence assessment.

Intersect will administer the funds through Sundae Labs treasury management smart contracts with specified TRSC and PSSC addresses, multi-party authorization rules, an external Oversight Committee, linked documentation, audits, repository references, and a public dashboard.

summary: The document requests 1,193,000 ADA for 12 months of Intersect Technical Steering Committee support, broken into three work packages for technical coordination, protocol governance, and technical review, with stated smart-contract fund administration, oversight, assurance, prior-funding disclosure, NCL compliance, and budget-process references.
